## Historical audit — S0166

**Scope:** Only chunk 1 of 5 is visible. All citations below refer to `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/sceneevolve_cli/C1/development/commons_109923183/trajectory.jsonl`. The reference and rendered images themselves are not visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observation and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1 | The stated goal was a separately meshed indoor reconstruction from one RGB image, matching viewpoint, framing, objects and materials without using the image as a texture. The student’s identification of a French chaise scene is an interpretation, not independently verified image content. |
| Student responses, lines 3 and 6 | The first program specified a paneled room, parquet, multipart chaise, pillow, label, curtains and foreground cane chair. After a pre-execution audit request, the student returned a revised complete program: it changed camera position, target and lens; changed parquet construction and pillow pose; reduced ornament; and added an upholstery grouping and material targeting. It also supplied estimated image bounds and wall/floor boundary. These are source-level changes, not verified appearance. |
| Student response, line 6; execute step 1, line 7 | The executed source includes separate frame, legs, head and arm components, custom upholstery meshes, procedural fabric and a rotated pillow. It attempts to parent upholstery to the chaise marker if found. Actual part contact, hierarchy, pose, texture appearance and occlusion cannot be established from source or object names alone. The code sets a camera, two area lights and a world; their visual adequacy is unknown. |
| Harness user message in student request, line 4; response line 6 | The visible intervention requested a **model-only source audit**, including radii, API use, material targeting and camera, expressly saying no render had occurred. The student subsequently produced a revised program, showing receipt and behavioral response; the trace does not show a separate teacher diagnosis or specific teacher-proposed fix. |
| Student CLI sessions, lines 2 and 5 | Both report zero tool calls. The initial construction and the prompted source revision are visible; no independent tool-based exploration is shown in those sessions. |
| Execute step 1, line 7; execution result line 8, characters [0,168793); select events lines 9–10 | The harness reports `ok: true`, no error, completion of 16 render samples and a saved image. Step 1 was selected twice. This establishes execution/render success and selection, not visual or geometric correctness. No student image comparison or rationale for selection is visible here. |

**Outcome and uncertainty:** The visible step succeeded technically; the overall reconstruction outcome is **unknown**, not established as formal visual success or failure. There is no evidence here of an empty patch or technical interruption. Whether camera framing, lighting, material appearance, object connections or the selected render match the photograph remains unresolved; later chunks cannot be inferred.

**Lessons:** Separating a preflight source audit from render validation is transferable: successful execution does not validate a scene’s appearance. The chaise geometry, parquet and chosen camera values are task-specific hypotheses, not generally validated solutions.
